issues.description: Most of the feature is uncommitted: the dropdown (templates/shifts.html:26), assignments.with_registration_status/candidates (assignments.py:36-47), the new tests (tests/test_journeys.py:52-85, tests/test_api.py:27-29) and the e2e scenario change (e2e/scenario.py:60-74) appear only in `git status`. The single commit 3352cde holds only part of the change.
issues.resolution: Commit the working-tree changes to app.py, assignments.py, e2e/scenario.py, templates/shifts.html, tests/test_api.py and tests/test_journeys.py on the feature branch before merging.

issues.description: app.py:156-159 (workers route) recomputes expiry with its own set comprehension over rules.registration_expired(data.to_rule_worker(...)) and passes an `expired` id set. The plan said to reuse the new assignments.with_registration_status helper. The same rule is now applied in two places.
issues.resolution: In app.py workers(), render with workers=assignments.with_registration_status(scope.workers(), clock.today()). Drop the `expired` set and the `import rules`. In templates/workers.html change the condition to `{% if worker.registration_expired %}`.

issues.description: README.md:41 and README.md:44 ('Pages and API' rows for GET /shifts and GET /workers) were not updated to mention the Expired label in the dropdown and the Expired badge, which the spec's 'Update the README' step requires.
issues.resolution: Edit README.md:41 to '...with an assign dropdown per open shift; workers whose registration has expired are shown as Expired and cannot be chosen'. Edit README.md:44 to 'workers with registration number and expiry, an Expired badge on expired registrations'.

issues.description: templates/workers.html:17 places the badge in the 'Registration expires' cell, not in the name cell as the plan said, and uses new .badge/.badge-expired classes (static/style.css:69-70) instead of reusing .status with .status-expired. The badge is still in the expired worker's row and next to the expiry date, as 05-workers.png shows.
issues.resolution: Optional: move the badge span into the name <td> and reuse `status status-expired` with a margin-left. Adjust the test strings in tests/test_journeys.py and the e2e selectors to match.

issues.description: The manifest includes a stale screenshot, 04-expired-refused.png, from the first e2e run (e2e.1.log). It shows the old 'Cannot assign Chloe Martin: Registration expired.' flow, which the current scenario no longer produces. The current run (e2e.2.log) writes 04-expired-unavailable.png instead.
issues.resolution: Clear e2e-results/ before each capture run so the manifest lists only screenshots from the final scenario.

issues.description: The workers() route in app.py:156-159 computes its own `expired` id set with rules.registration_expired + data.to_rule_worker. The spec said to use the new assignments.with_registration_status (assignments.py:36-39). The 'is this worker expired' logic now lives in two places, and app.py gains a direct `import rules` (app.py:24).
issues.resolution: In app.py workers(), render with `workers=assignments.with_registration_status(scope.workers(), clock.today())` and drop the `expired` set and the `import rules`. In templates/workers.html:17, test `worker.registration_expired` instead of `worker.id in expired`. tests/test_journeys.py needs no changes.

issues.description: README.md was not updated, although the spec's 'Update the README' step asks for it. The 'Pages and API' rows for GET /shifts (manager) and GET /workers say nothing about the Expired label, the disabled option or the badge.
issues.resolution: In the README.md 'Pages and API' table, add to GET /shifts (manager): 'workers whose registration has expired are shown as Expired and cannot be chosen'. Add to GET /workers: 'an Expired badge on expired registrations'.

issues.description: Most of the change is still uncommitted: git status shows app.py, assignments.py, e2e/scenario.py, templates/shifts.html, tests/test_api.py and tests/test_journeys.py as modified. Commit 3352cde holds only part of it, and on its own the committed part has the dropdown e2e step but none of the disabled-option work.
issues.resolution: Commit the working-tree changes on branch feature/8d4e8d6a-mark-workers-whose-registration-has-expired, so the branch head matches the reviewed code and the artefacts.

issues.description: The manifest still lists 04-expired-refused.png from the first e2e run (e2e.1.log), from before the option was disabled. It shows the old 'Cannot assign Chloe Martin: Registration expired.' flash and is not produced by the current scenario (e2e.2.log). Also, 06-workers-expired-badge.png has the same sha256 as 05-workers.png, because the extra 'wait 400' step at e2e/scenario.py:72-74 adds a check but no new picture.
issues.resolution: Clear e2e-results/ before collecting artefacts, so stale screenshots from earlier runs are not carried into the manifest. Optionally drop the 'screenshot' key from the badge-count step at e2e/scenario.py:72-74, since it repeats the 'workers' screenshot.

issues.description: The badge is in the 'Registration expires' cell (templates/workers.html:17), with class `badge badge-expired`. The spec planned it in the name cell, with class `status status-expired`. It is still in the expired worker's row and only there, so the criterion holds (see 05-workers.png).
issues.resolution: No change needed. If you want to match the spec exactly, move the span after `{{ worker.name }}` in the first <td> and reuse the `.status` pill class.

combined_verdict.summary: The change marks workers whose registration has expired. The workers page shows a red 'Expired' badge in the expired worker's row. In the shifts-board dropdown the expired worker is labelled 'Name (Expired)' and the option is disabled. The server-side refusal in rules.py, the API and worker_json is untouched. Every acceptance criterion is met and proved: tests pass (51 passed, 16 passed for isolation, no failures or skips), the e2e run passes, 04-expired-unavailable.png and keyframe session-04 show 'Chloe Martin (Expired)' greyed out in the #assign-8 list, and 05/06 screenshots and keyframes 06-08 show the badge on Chloe Martin only. Much of the change (assignments.py, shifts.html, tests, scenario.py) is still uncommitted in the worktree. The deviations from the plan are not blocking. | The change adds an 'Expired' badge on the workers page (templates/workers.html:17, computed in app.py:156-159) and shows expired workers as a disabled 'Name (Expired)' option in the assign dropdown (assignments.py:36-46, templates/shifts.html:26, app.py:122-124). rules.py, the assign/API paths and the existing refusal tests are unchanged, and no protected path is touched. All five acceptance criteria are met. The proof: 04-expired-unavailable.png and keyframe session-04.png show 'Chloe Martin (Expired)' greyed out in #assign-8 with Amara Jones, Daniel Reyes and Sam Okafor selectable; 05-workers.png and keyframes session-06 to session-08 show a red Expired badge beside Chloe Martin only; test.2.log reports 51 passed, isolation.2.log 16 passed and e2e.2.log 'passed, 9 steps'. What is left is small: the workers route duplicates the new helper, the README was not updated, part of the work is not committed, and the manifest holds a stale screenshot from an earlier run.
